title: C3: vanishing of p-primary torsion
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed with
$\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, let $C$ be a
smooth separated connected curve over $k$, and let
$n=p$. Then the constant sheaf $\mathbf F_p$ satisfies
$\mathcal C_3(C,\mathbf F_p)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]: for every $q>1$,
$H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_p)=0$.

proof.text: The hypotheses on k and C are exactly those of [lem-sc-artin-schreier-dimension]. Applying that lemma to the constant étale sheaf F_p gives H^q(C_et,F_p)=0 for each integer q>1. Its Artin–Schreier argument is carried by that node; no assertion about arbitrary p-primary sheaves is needed here.

Multiplication by p on the constant sheaf F_p is zero, so this sheaf is p-primary. The characteristic-p clause C_3 in [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] asks precisely for the vanishings just obtained. Thus C_3(C,F_p) holds.
